source_type: Official University of Macau Global Affairs Office International Student Scholarship and AY2026/2027 admission sources
funding_classification_basis: The official University of Macau International Student Scholarship for AY2026/2027 onward contains multiple award tiers. Bachelor Full Scholarship provides 100% tuition and 100% Residential College accommodation waiver, while Half Scholarship provides 50% of each. Master's Type A provides 100% tuition, 100% on-campus accommodation and a MOP 4,000 monthly half teaching assistantship; Type B provides 100% tuition; Type C provides an international tuition differential waiver. EduPath therefore stores Variable Funding instead of incorrectly presenting every recipient as fully funded.
unresolved_fields: individual scholarship tier before admission evaluation
universal monthly allowance because only Master's Type A receives MOP 4,000 per month
universal accommodation coverage because coverage differs by award tier
single application opening date because Bachelor and Master admission routes differ
single scholarship deadline because scholarship consideration is automatic and linked to different admission routes
eligibility_basis: Eligible applicants are international applicants holding valid foreign passports who apply to eligible full-time Bachelor's or Master's degree programmes and satisfy the programme admission requirements. No separate scholarship application is required; eligible applicants are automatically considered during admission evaluation.
status_basis: AY2026/2027 Bachelor direct admission ran from 3 February to 9 April 2026. Standard Master's admission ran through 13 March 2026, with the Master of Design in Industrial Design accepting applications until 15 May 2026. These associated AY2026/2027 admission windows had all ended by the 23 August 2026 verification date, so this cycle is recorded as closed.
notes: No artificial nationality list, universal GPA threshold, universal English score or universal stipend is created. Degree-specific admission requirements and award-tier-specific financial benefits remain represented conservatively.
